samples.summary: `docStore.snapshot()` immediately followed by `doc.batch(...)` produces TWO undo checkpoints under `MemDocStore`, contradicting the store's documented "one action = one undo unit" contract
samples.evidence: The new in-place link edit does `docStore.snapshot(); … doc.batch(() => {…})` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1202-1225 and the mirror in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3620-3656). Out of diff: `MemDocStore.snapshot()` only skips its `pushUndo()` when `batchDepth > 0` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:177-184), and `MemDocStore.batch()` unconditionally pushes its own `before` clone when `batchDepth === 0` (memory.ts:206-210). Ordering snapshot *before* batch therefore pushes two identical checkpoints, i.e. one link-href edit costs two undo presses (`canUndo()` stays true after the first, memory.ts:169). The established pattern in this very package is the inverse — `withNamedStyleChange` does `doc.batch(() => { docStore.snapshot(); … })` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1236-1245), and `DocStore.batch`'s contract note says one top-level batch is at most one undo unit (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:64-66). `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2918) so the frontend docs editor is unaffected; the text-box editor (always `MemDocStore`, undo exposed at text-box-editor.ts:1296) and the MemDocStore harness/CLI paths are. Fix belongs on the new code: move `docStore.snapshot()` inside the `doc.batch` body.

samples.summary: The new "a link is an atomic selection unit" rule is wired only into the body pointer paths; the header/footer drag path and the docs text-box editor's own drag still store partially-covering ranges
samples.evidence: `expandRangeForLinks` is applied through `setSnappedRange` at text-editor.ts:2016, 2067 and 2353 only. Out of diff, `updateDragSelection`'s header/footer branch writes the range directly with `this.selection.setRange({ anchor: this.selection.range.anchor, focus: pos })` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2225) — no snap, and unlike the shift+arrow divergence at text-editor.ts:3186-3194 this one carries no comment, so it reads as an oversight. The docs text-box editor keeps its own `Selection` (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:480) and never snaps or sets `rawAnchor` either, so the same gesture over the same link behaves differently in a text box. Nothing downstream crashes (no consumer asserts the invariant), so this is a consistency gap rather than a break.

samples.summary: The new Apply guard keys off "the prefill was non-empty" and then requires a caret-in-link, so it silently discards an Apply that the old code would have applied to a live selection
samples.evidence: `handleApply` now returns early whenever `editingExistingLink && !editor.getLinkAtCursor()` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:152-156), and `editingExistingLink` is set purely from a non-empty prefill (line 88), which `docs-view.tsx:465` derives from `getLinkAtCursor()` — a caret-only probe. But `EditorAPI.insertLink` has a selection branch that does not need the caret to be inside a link at all (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3582-3611): ⌘K opened on a link, then a new selection dragged elsewhere while the popover deliberately stays open, used to link that selection and now does nothing at all, with no feedback. Confirmed only one caller of `insertLink` exists (docs-link-popover.tsx:157), so there is no bypass of the guard — only this over-reach. Fix belongs on the new guard: also let the range branch through (e.g. skip the guard when `editor.getActiveSelection()` is non-null).

samples.summary: The in-place link behaviour change to the docs text-box editor propagates into the slides package through its re-exported `insertLink`
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:634-641` wraps `initializeTextBox` from @wafflebase/docs and forwards `insertLink`/`getLinkAtCursor` verbatim, so a URL-labelled link's *text* now changes on an href edit in slides text boxes too. Nothing in packages/frontend/src/app/slides currently calls it (only the note at slides-view.tsx:739 and test stubs), so impact today is nil, but the slides-side API doc (docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:262) still describes it as an href mutation.
